definitions.definitionEn: A collection of objects, together with a transitively closed collection of composable arrows between them, such that every object has an identity arrow, and such that arrow composition is associative.

example.en: Just as a monoid consists of an underlying set with a binary operation "on top of it" which is closed, associative and with an identity, a category consists of an underlying digraph with an arrow composition operation "on top of it" which is transitively closed, associative, and with an identity at each object. In fact, a category's composition operation, when restricted to a single one of its objects, turns that object's set of arrows (which would all be loops) into a monoid.
example.ja: モノイドとは、二次元の操作で「その上」に「その上の」と「アイデンティティー」が組み込まれている基礎集合であるように、カテゴリは「その上に」矢印の組成操作で、各オブジェクトの個人情報を移転させたものである. 事実、カテゴリの構成処理は、一つのオブジェクトに限定したときは、そのオブジェクトの矢印(すべてはループしている)を単独化させる。

example.en: The gun had obviously been placed in her car in an effort to frame her.
example.ja: 明らかに、銃は彼女を刺そうとして車の中に置かれていました。

definitions.definitionEn: To wash ore with the aid of a frame.
To move.
To proceed; to go.
To hit (the ball) with the frame of the racquet rather than the strings (normally a mishit).
To strengthen; refresh; support.
To execute; perform.

example.en: All have sworn him an oath that they should frame his will on earth.
example.ja: すべての人は、地上で神のご意志を定めるという誓いを立てました。

definitions.definitionEn: To cause; to bring about; to produce.
To profit; avail.
To fit; accord.
To succeed in doing or trying to do something; manage.
(manner) At a slow pace.

meaning: 〈C〉縛る物 / 《通例複数形で》束縛,拘束,かせ / 《しばしば複数形で》(血縁,義理などの)きずな,縁 / 〈C〉契約 / 〈C〉証書,証文;債券,公債 / 〈U〉(石・れんがなどの)つなぎ方,組積み / 〈U〉保税倉庫入り / 〈U〉接着,接合;接着剤,接合剤 / 〈品物〉を担保とする / …の保証人となる / (債券などを発行して)…の支払いを保証する / …をつなぐ,結ぶ(bind together) / つながる

definitions.definitionEn: Evidence of a long-term debt, by which the bond issuer (the borrower) is obliged to pay interest when due, and repay the principal at maturity, as specified on the face of the bond certificate. The rights of the holder are specified in the bond indenture, which contains the legal terms and conditions under which the bond was issued. Bonds are available in two forms: registered bonds, and bearer bonds.
A documentary obligation to pay a sum or to perform a contract; a debenture.

example.en: Investors face a quandary. Cash offers a return of virtually zero in many developed countries; government-bond yields may have risen in recent weeks but they are still unattractive. Equities have suffered two big bear markets since 2000 and are wobbling again. It is hardly surprising that pension funds, insurers and endowments are searching for new sources of return.
example.ja: 参業者は、高額な投資を行っており、多くの先進国において、現金は実質的にゼロの返還を申し出ているが、ここ数週間で政府に定める収入は増加しているかもしれないが、まだ不便な状態だ。経済は2000年以降2つの大きな熊の市場に苦しんだが、再び急激している。

definitions.definitionEn: A partial payment made to show a provider that the customer is sincere about buying a product or a service. If the product or service is not purchased the customer then forfeits the bond.
(often in the plural) A physical connection which binds, a band.

example.en: The prisoner was brought before the tribunal in iron bonds.
example.ja: 囚人は鉄の債券で裁判所に連れて行かれました。

definitions.definitionEn: An emotional link, connection or union; that which holds two or more people together, as in a friendship; a tie.

example.en: They had grown up as friends and neighbors, and not even vastly differing political views could break the bond of their friendship.
example.ja: 彼らは友人や隣人として成長しており、政治的な見解が大きく異なっていても、友情の絆を砕くことはできませんでした。

definitions.definitionEn: Moral or political duty or obligation.
A link or force between neighbouring atoms in a molecule.

example.en: Organic chemistry primarily consists of the study of carbon bonds, in their many variations.
example.ja: 有機化学はおもに、様々な種類の炭素結合を研究することによって構成されます。

definitions.definitionEn: A binding agreement, a covenant.

example.en: Herbert resented his wife for subjecting him to the bonds of matrimony; he claimed they had gotten married while drunk.
example.ja: ハーバートは妻に対して、結婚の絆を強めたことで腹を立て、酔っている間に結婚したと言いました。

definitions.definitionEn: A bail bond.

example.en: The bailiff released the prisoner as soon as the bond was posted.
example.ja: 保釈金が提出されるとすぐにその囚人を釈放した。

definitions.definitionEn: Any constraining or cementing force or material.

example.en: A bond of superglue adhered the teacups to the ceiling, much to the consternation of the cafe owners.
example.ja: 喫茶店の持ち主は、ティーカップを天井にくっつけていました。

definitions.definitionEn: In building, a specific pattern of bricklaying.
In Scotland, a mortgage.
A heavy copper wire or rod connecting adjacent rails of an electric railway track when used as a part of the electric circuit.
To connect, secure or tie with a bond; to bind.

example.en: The gargantuan ape was bonded in iron chains and carted onto the stage.
example.ja: ガガントゥアン猿は鉄の鎖で縛られ、舞台に積まれていた。

definitions.definitionEn: To cause to adhere (one material with another).

example.en: The children bonded their snapshots to the scrapbook pages with mucilage.
example.ja: 子供たちはスナップ写真をスクラップブックのページに貼り付け、そのページには粘り気がありました。

definitions.definitionEn: To form a chemical compound with.

example.en: Under unusual conditions, even gold can be made to bond with other elements.
example.ja: 異常な状況のもとでは、金でさえ他の元素と結合させることができます。

definitions.definitionEn: To guarantee or secure a financial risk.

example.en: The contractor was bonded with a local underwriter.
example.ja: 請負業者は地方のアンダーライターと結びついていた。

definitions.definitionEn: To form a friendship or emotional connection.

example.en: The men had bonded while serving together in Vietnam.
example.ja: 男たちはベトナムで共に奉仕していた時に絆を結んでいました。

definitions.definitionEn: To put in a bonded warehouse; to secure (goods) until the associated duties are paid.
To lay bricks in a specific pattern.
To make a reliable electrical connection between two conductors (or any pieces of metal that may potentially become conductors).

example.en: A house's distribution panel should always be bonded to the grounding rods via a panel bond.
example.ja: 家の配送パネルは、常にパネルの結合を通じて地面棒に縛るべきである。

definitions.definitionEn: To bail out by means of a bail bond.
A peasant; churl.
A vassal; serf; one held in bondage to a superior.
Subject to the tenure called bondage.
In a state of servitude or slavedom; not free.
Servile; slavish; pertaining to or befitting a slave.

example.en: bond fear
example.ja: 連帯不安

meaning: 〈人〉を雇う / (金を払って)〈物〉を借りる,賃借する / 〈物〉を賃貸しする;〈自分〉が金で雇われる《+out+名,+名+out》 / 借り賃,使用料;雇い賃,給料 / (物の)賃貸し,賃借り;(人の)雇用 / (人が)雇われて

definitions.definitionEn: Payment for the temporary use of something.

example.en: The sign offered pedalos on hire.
example.ja: その看板にはペトラスが雇っていました。

definitions.definitionEn: Reward, payment.
The state of being hired, or having a job; employment.

example.en: When my grandfather retired, he had over twenty mechanics in his hire.
example.ja: 祖父は退職した時には、雇い主が 20 人以上いました。

definitions.definitionEn: A person who has been hired, especially in a cohort.

example.en: We pair up each of our new hires with one of our original hires.
example.ja: 新しい雇用者ごとに元の雇用者とペアを組ます

definitions.definitionEn: To obtain the services of in return for fixed payment.

example.en: We hired a car for two weeks because ours had broken down.
example.ja: 私たちは自分たちの車が故障していたので、 2 週間車を借りました。

definitions.definitionEn: To employ; to obtain the services of (a person) in exchange for remuneration; to give someone a job.

example.en: The company had problems when it tried to hire more skilled workers.
example.ja: その会社は、より多くの熟練した労働者を雇おうとして、問題を抱えていました。

definitions.definitionEn: To exchange the services of for remuneration.

example.en: They hired themselves out as day laborers.  They hired out their basement for Inauguration week.
example.ja: 彼らはその日の労働者として自営し、土屋を土曜に買収した。

definitions.definitionEn: To accomplish by paying for services.

example.en: After waiting two years for her husband to finish the tiling, she decided to hire it done.
example.ja: 夫がトリングを完成するまで 2 年間待った後、妻はそれを雇うことにしました。

definitions.definitionEn: To accept employment.

example.en: They hired out as day laborers.
example.ja: 労働者として雇った

meaning: (壁などにあいた)穴,割れ目;(衣類などの)破れ穴,裂け目;(道路などにできた)くぼみ,へこみ / (動物の住む)巣穴 / 《話》あばら家 / (議論・計画などの)欠点(fault) / 《話》窮地,苦境 / ホール(ゴルフで球を打ち込む穴);(球をホールに入れた)得点 / 〈物〉に穴をあける(掘る) / (ゴルフで)〈球〉を打ってホールに入れる(ゴルフで)球を打ってホールに入れる《+out》

definitions.definitionEn: A hollow place or cavity; an excavation; a pit; an opening in or through a solid body, a fabric, etc.; a perforation; a rent; a fissure.

example.en: There’s a hole in my shoe.  Her stocking has a hole in it.
example.ja: 靴の中には穴が開いています。

definitions.definitionEn: (heading) In games.
An excavation pit or trench.
A weakness; a flaw or ambiguity.

example.en: I have found a hole in your argument.
example.ja: あなたの言い分に穴を見つけたわ

definitions.definitionEn: A container or receptacle.

example.en: car hole;  brain hole
example.ja: 車の穴; 脳の穴

definitions.definitionEn: In semiconductors, a lack of an electron in an occupied band behaving like a positively charged particle.
A security vulnerability in software which can be taken advantage of by an exploit.
An orifice, in particular the anus. When used with shut it always refers to the mouth.

example.en: Just shut your hole!
example.ja: ドアを閉めろ!

definitions.definitionEn: (particularly in the phrase "get one's hole") Sex, or a sex partner.

example.en: Are you going out to get your hole tonight?
example.ja: 今夜穴を開けるの?

definitions.definitionEn: (with "the") Solitary confinement, a high-security prison cell often used as punishment.
An undesirable place to live or visit; a hovel.

example.en: His apartment is a hole!
example.ja: 彼のアパートは穴だ!

definitions.definitionEn: Difficulty, in particular, debt.

example.en: If you find yourself in a hole, stop digging.
example.ja: 穴の中にいる自分に気づいたなら、穴を掘るのをやめてください。

definitions.definitionEn: A chordless cycle in a graph.
To make holes in (an object or surface).

example.en: Shrapnel holed the ship's hull.
example.ja: シュラプネルは船体に穴をあけた

definitions.definitionEn: (by extension) To destroy.

example.en: She completely holed the argument.
example.ja: 彼女はその論議を完全に封じました。

definitions.definitionEn: To go into a hole.
To drive into a hole, as an animal, or a billiard ball or golf ball.

example.en: Woods holed a standard three foot putt
example.ja: 木は標準的な 3 メートルの穴を埋めている

definitions.definitionEn: To cut, dig, or bore a hole or holes in.

example.en: to hole a post for the insertion of rails or bars
example.ja: レールやバーの挿入のための柱をホールドする

definitions.definitionEn: Entire, undivided.

example.en: I ate a whole fish.
example.ja: 魚を丸ごと食べた。

definitions.definitionEn: Sound, uninjured, healthy.

example.en: He is of whole mind, but the same cannot be said about his physical state.
example.ja: その人は頭の中では全く考えていますが、自分の身体的な状態についても同じことが言えません。

definitions.definitionEn: (of food) From which none of its constituents has been removed.

example.en: whole wheat; whole milk
example.ja: 小麦全体; ミルク全体

definitions.definitionEn: As yet unworked.
